chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah — from Muhammad ibn Abi Yusr — from Dawud ibn Abdillah — from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Muhammad — from Isa ibn Yunus, who said:

Ibn Abi al-Awja was among the students of al-Hasan al-Basri, but he deviated from monotheism. It was said to him: 'You have abandoned the school of your teacher and entered into something that has no foundation.' He said: 'My teacher was confused; sometimes he would speak of predestination (qadar), and sometimes he would say: the matter is not up to me. I do not know the truth of his affair.'

When he arrived at the House — meaning during the season of pilgrimage — he saw the people in their circumambulation, their running, and their supplications, and he said: 'O Abu Abdillah, who are these people who circle around this stone, rub themselves against it, and rush toward it like the rushing of the wind? Are these not people of reason?'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'These are the ones whom Allah intended from among His servants, and He made this House into watering places for the drawing of their religious obligations. Then they frequented it as the station of His prophets, and He beckoned them toward competing in closeness to Him, and He thickened its structure so that it would be a symbol for the continuance of worship in honor of it. It is the place of response for those who answered Him from the ancients and the latter ones. There is no believer except that his heart yearns toward it and longs for it.'

'Do you not know that Allah loves to be obeyed from where He has commanded and to be feared where He has forbidden, and it is not for anyone to go beyond His command to something other than His command? Have you not heard Allah say: "And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers"?' He (the narrator) said: Ibn Abi al-Awja gave him no response.

key_terms.مَنَاهِل: watering places / wellsprings of religious duty

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq respond to the atheist Ibn Abi al-Awja's challenge about the Ka'ba?
ai.summary: The famous atheist and freethinker Ibn Abi al-Awja, a former student of al-Hasan al-Basri who had deviated from monotheism, challenged Imam al-Sadiq (AS) during the Hajj season, mocking the pilgrims for their devotion to the Ka'ba stone. The Imam responded with a profound theological defense, explaining that the Ka'ba is divinely appointed as a spiritual center for humanity — a station of prophets, a watering place for religious duties, and a symbol of perpetual worship — concluding with the Quranic verse that only Islam is accepted by Allah, leaving Ibn Abi al-Awja speechless.
